transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because something happened at work. I got really worked up during a staff meeting and started acting out a whole fall-prevention drill, moving chairs around and waving my arms like I was demonstrating it. I couldn’t really stop, even when people were telling me to sit down. It was embarrassing, and I guess it worried them too.
Has anything like that happened to you before?

Yeah… I mean, the work thing is the main one I can think of right now. I got really worked up in that meeting and started acting out the whole fall-prevention drill, moving chairs around and waving my arms like I was showing everybody. People told me to sit down, but I just couldn’t seem to stop myself right then.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Yeah… I keep thinking about my supervisor and a couple people at work. Even when I’m calm, I still feel like they’re keeping notes on me or testing me with little comments. Like they’re trying to prove I’m not safe to be around the seniors.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

Yeah… sometimes I do. Like if I’m alone in the hallway at work, or at home near the laundry room, I’ll hear my name or hear a resident calling for help, clear as day. But when I go check, there’s nobody there.
How long have you been hearing voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?
I’d say it’s been about nine months now. The hearing calls or my name when nobody’s there… that started around the same time as me feeling suspicious about people at work.
Do you find it hard to express your thoughts in a way that makes sense to others, or do you feel like your thoughts are disjointed?

Yeah, sometimes. My thoughts move too fast. I’ll start thinking about work, then it jumps to church, then my wife, then some idea for a workshop or something… and by the time I try to explain it, I lose the first thing I was trying to say. So it can come out mixed up.
When you're thinking about something, do you usually feel like you can follow your own train of thought from start to finish?

Not usually, no. I’ll start on one thing, like my job, and then my mind jumps to church, then to my wife, then some idea for a workshop. It goes so fast I lose what I was first trying to say before I can get it out right.
Have you noticed any other times when your behavior seemed really disorganized or unpredictable to you or others?

Yeah… the big one was at work. I got really worked up during a staff meeting and started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill, moving chairs around and waving my arms like I was showing everybody what to do. I couldn’t really stop myself, even when people were telling me to sit down.
Do you really believe that your supervisor and coworkers are keeping notes on you or testing you, or is that just a suspicion that crosses your mind sometimes?

I mean… I really do believe it. It’s not just a quick thought that comes and goes. Even when I’m calm, I still feel like my supervisor and a couple people there are keeping notes on me, watching how I act, and making little comments to test me. Like they’re trying to prove I’m not safe to be around the seniors.
Do you think the voices you hear are real?

At the time, yeah, they feel real. Like, I’ll be alone in the hallway or at home by the laundry room and I hear my name, or a resident calling for help, clear as day. But when I go check, there’s nobody there.
Do you think the belief that your supervisor and coworkers are keeping notes on you is something that might not be true?

I guess I can say maybe it’s possible, but honestly, even when I’m calm, I still feel pretty sure they’re doing it. My supervisor and a couple coworkers… it feels like they’re watching me, keeping notes, making little comments to test me, like they’re trying to show I’m not safe to be around the seniors.
Do you often find yourself having trouble sticking to one topic when talking to others?

Yeah, I do. Sometimes when I’m talking, my mind jumps around so fast—like I’ll start about my job, then suddenly I’m thinking about church, then my wife, then some idea for a workshop. By the time I try to explain it, I kind of lose the first thought and don’t say it right.
Do you have trouble completing tasks or projects at home because your thoughts are disorganized?

Yeah… at home I do. My wife says I’ll just sit in the living room staring at the TV with the volume real low, and I don’t get up to do things. Simple chores, like stuff I know needs to be done, I just don’t finish them like I used to. I don’t even call people from church much anymore.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with family, friends, or coworkers since these experiences started?

Yeah, it’s caused problems. I got put on leave from the senior center, so that’s been hard. At home, my wife has to remind me about chores and appointments because I’m not keeping up like I used to.

And I’ve pulled back from people at church too. I don’t talk to them much. I just worry a lot about whether I can even go back to caregiving work safely.
Do you think the beliefs you have about your supervisor and coworkers are definitely true, or can you consider the possibility that they might not be?

Honestly… I feel pretty sure it’s true. Even when I’m calm and I try to think it through, I still feel like my supervisor and a couple people at work are keeping notes on me. Like they make these little comments to test me, to see if I’m safe around the seniors or not. I know you’re asking if maybe I could be wrong, but it doesn’t really feel like that to me.
Are the voices you hear most of the time, or are they rare?

Not most of the time, no. It’s more like it happens sometimes… like if I’m alone in the hallway or at home near the laundry room, I’ll hear my name or hear a resident calling for help, clear as day. But then I check, and there’s nobody there.
Do you think the people at work are trying to harm you or plot against you, rather than just testing you?

I don’t know if I’d say they’re trying to hurt me, exactly. It feels more like they’re watching me and keeping notes, trying to catch me slipping up. Like my supervisor and a couple others make little comments to test me, to prove I’m not safe around the seniors. Even when I calm down, I still feel pretty sure that’s what’s going on.
When you think about your supervisor and coworkers keeping notes on you, how realistic does that seem to you - is it something that could actually happen in your workplace?

Yeah… to me it feels realistic. I mean, at my job people do write things down, and supervisors watch how you work, so it doesn’t seem far-fetched to me. Even when I calm myself down, I still feel sure my supervisor and a couple people are keeping notes on me and making little comments to test me, like they’re trying to prove I’m not safe around the seniors.
Are the voices you hear usually the main thing you're experiencing when you're having a hard time, or is it more the suspicious thoughts about your supervisor and coworkers?

It’s more the suspicious thoughts, I think. The voices happen sometimes, but when I’m really having a hard time, it’s mostly that feeling that my supervisor and a couple people are keeping notes on me, testing me with little comments. Even if I’m calm, I still feel pretty sure they’re trying to prove I’m not safe around the seniors.
Do you think your thoughts about your supervisor and coworkers are connected to the other times when you've had trouble making sense or following through on things?

I’m not sure if they’re connected. When I’m having trouble keeping things straight, it might make me more focused on it, but even when I’m calm I still feel sure my supervisor and a couple people are keeping notes on me. Like they make little comments to test me, to show I’m not safe around the seniors.
